title: Column Totals

illustrates.quote: b. When horizontal lines separate column items from totals, the horizontal line symbol should extend across the width of the column total. (See Sample 11-8: Column Totals on page 11-33.)

print.caption: EXAMPLE BASE PRICE METHOD
print.notes: "Raw Food Costs"/"37%" values are each underscored by a short horizontal rule, and "Customer's Meal Cost"/"$35.00"/"100%" is the total row below that rule (sum of Profit+Overhead+Labor+Raw Food Costs).
print.printFeatures: No box border; centered bold caption above a plain (unboxed) table; thin horizontal rules under the "12.95" and "37%" entries only, marking them as the last addend before the total.

braille.notes: Line 1 placeholder "text". No box lines are used (table is not enclosed in a box, consistent with the unboxed print original). The horizontal rule under "Raw Food Costs"/"37%" in print is rendered in braille as a run of horizontal-line-symbol dots (the two grey-highlighted '.........' / '.......' groups on line 9) extending across the width of each of those two columns only, per rule 11.6.2.b, immediately above the total row.
